chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abbad ibn Suhayb, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The apostate is asked to repent; if he repents, [he is spared], and if not, he is killed. He said: And the woman is asked to repent; if she repents, [she is spared], and if not, she is imprisoned in prison and confined.

key_terms.يُسْتَتَابُ: He is asked to repent / invited to repent

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in punishment for male and female apostates in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al--Istibsar establishes the foundational Shia distinction in the punishment for apostasy, where men face execution after a period of invitation to repent (istitab), while women are subject to imprisonment and confinement rather than death. This ruling reflects the juristic view that female apostates do not require the same capital penalty as males, often linked to differences in combatant status or financial liability in classical fiqh. The text highlights the procedural emphasis on giving the apostate a chance to return to Islam before the final penalty is enacted.
